findings.title: unsubscribe dereferences a possibly nil TopicUser
findings.body: `TopicUser.find_by(...)` returns nil when the user has no topic_users row for this topic, for example a user who received a mailing-list email without ever visiting the topic. `tu.notification_level` then raises NoMethodError and the request returns a 500. Use `TopicUser.change`, or create the row first, so the unsubscribe still works.

findings.title: State change on a GET request with no CSRF protection
findings.body: The unsubscribe action mutates the notification level on a GET request, so any link or image tag can trigger it. Mail scanners and link prefetchers that follow the link in the email will also mute or unwatch the topic without the user asking. The action also changes the level on every visit, not just once: a second visit flips regular to muted.

findings.title: Guardian access check is missing for the topic
findings.body: `TopicView.new(params[:topic_id], current_user)` is created without `check_and_raise_exceptions`, and the code never calls `guardian.ensure_can_see!`. The code also reads `@topic_view.topic` before any permission check.

findings.title: Misspelled property name `stopNotificiationsText`
findings.body: `stopNotificiationsText` is misspelled, and the template repeats the typo. It works only because the two match. The name should be fixed before it becomes API.

findings.title: Triple-stash renders the topic title unescaped
findings.body: `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` renders unescaped HTML that interpolates `model.fancyTitle`. This is probably safe only because `fancyTitle` is escaped server-side, but `I18n.t` interpolation of user-controlled titles into raw HTML is fragile.

findings.title: Template path does not match the route name
findings.body: The route is `topicUnsubscribe`, but the template is placed at `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`. Ember resolves `topicUnsubscribe` to `templates/topicUnsubscribe` or `topic-unsubscribe`, so this template will probably not be found.

findings.title: `unsubscribe_link` now needs `%{unsubscribe_url}` but not all callers pass it
findings.body: The `unsubscribe_link` string now requires `%{unsubscribe_url}`, but only `send_notification_email` passes it. Other users of `add_unsubscribe_link` would raise an I18n missing-interpolation error. The text body also appends the string with `<<` onto what may be a frozen translation.
